author: Juan lacruz
symmetry_note: Best symmetry in the set. Estimated shoulder-to-wingtip distances left:right about 1.03 (about 600 vs 620 px in the 2000 px view, +/-5 pct). Both wings fully extended, both tips and all primaries visible, tail fully fanned. Bird is nose-up toward camera so head and body are foreshortened (body length understated), wings roughly perpendicular to line of sight. Near-uniform pale grey-lavender sky.
why_kept: Symmetric spread wings plus fully fanned tail on uniform sky; adult/juvenile uncertain but peregrine malar and helmet visible at 3.6x.
species_check: In Commons category 'Falco peregrinus in flight' (or Commons description says Peregrine); peregrine field marks (black helmet/malar, barred or streaked underparts, barred tail) confirmed on 3.6x crop of head/tail; no kestrel/hobby/other falcon features.

author: Channel City Camera Club from Santa Barbara, US (credit line in description: Photo: Steve Colwell)
subspecies_or_sex_if_stated: not stated (adult plumage; Lake Los Carneros, Santa Barbara CA)
symmetry_note: Both wings fully extended with all primaries visible; left wing about 15-20 pct longer than right in the image (shoulder-to-tip about 490 vs 410 px), so mild yaw/foreshortening of the right wing. Wings swept back slightly; tail partly fanned (about 5 feathers spread); feet tucked over tail base. Saturated uniform blue sky, highest contrast of the set.
why_kept: Clean soaring pose, adult head and tail pattern clear, easiest sky to segment; mild asymmetry noted.
species_check: In Commons category 'Falco peregrinus in flight' (or Commons description says Peregrine); peregrine field marks (black helmet/malar, barred or streaked underparts, barred tail) confirmed on 4.0x crop of head/tail; no kestrel/hobby/other falcon features.

author: lwolfartist
symmetry_note: Wings spread and swept back, left:right shoulder-to-tip about 1.06 (about 390 vs 410 px in the 1280 px view), both tips visible; image rotated about 30 deg in plane; head and neck foreshortened (nose toward camera); tail closed. Bird wingspan only about 800 px in the 1718 px original (bird fills a small part of frame).
why_kept: Near-symmetric closed-tail glide on plain blue sky.
species_check: In Commons category 'Falco peregrinus in flight' (or Commons description says Peregrine); peregrine field marks (black helmet/malar, barred or streaked underparts, barred tail) confirmed on 3.0x crop of body/tail (streaked juvenile, malar visible); no kestrel/hobby/other falcon features.

symmetry_note: Wings swept back and level, upper:lower shoulder-to-tip about 1.05 (about 580 vs 555 px), both tips visible; bird oriented almost vertically in the frame; tail closed and squared. species_check: In Commons category 'Falco peregrinus in flight' (or Commons description says Peregrine); peregrine field marks (black helmet/malar, barred or streaked underparts, barred tail) confirmed on 3.1x crop of tail/head; no kestrel/hobby/other falcon features.

author: Benjamin Smith from United States
subspecies_or_sex_if_stated: female (stated in title; banded bird, Grand Forks ND)
symmetry_note: Wings fully extended and symmetric (upper:lower shoulder-to-tip about 1.0, about 407 vs 408 px), both tips visible, slight rearward sweep, tail broad and slightly fanned with dark terminal band. BACKGROUND IS THIN CLOUD: dark wings segment well, but pale throat and belly have low contrast against pale cloud.
why_kept: Good large symmetric planform; downgraded only for cloud background.
species_check: In Commons category 'Falco peregrinus in flight' (or Commons description says Peregrine); peregrine field marks (black helmet/malar, barred or streaked underparts, barred tail) confirmed on 4.3x crop of head/tail; no kestrel/hobby/other falcon features.

symmetry_note: Wings swept back and symmetric (upper:lower about 1.01, about 342 vs 338 px), both tips visible, tail closed and narrow. Bird spans only about 770 px of the 1985 px frame, so wing detail is small. Flickr copy at 1985 px.

author: Jimmyc2023
symmetry_note: Wings extended and symmetric (about 302 vs 309 px shoulder-to-tip), both tips visible; bird flying toward camera so body and tail are foreshortened (tail length unreliable); light uniform blue sky. Bird spans only about 650 px in the 1332 px original.
why_kept: Clean sky and symmetric wings; limited by bird size and foreshortened tail.
species_check: In Commons category 'Falco peregrinus in flight' (or Commons description says Peregrine); peregrine field marks (black helmet/malar, barred or streaked underparts, barred tail) confirmed on 8.3x crop of head/tail; no kestrel/hobby/other falcon features.

author: Mike Baird
symmetry_note: Both wings fully extended with tips drooping slightly and swept back; head-on from below with a mild bank: right wing about 15 pct longer in the image than left (about 846 vs 737 px). Tail foreshortened and closed. Wing camber could mean the end of a downstroke, but both wings are level and outstretched so treated as a glide. Plain pale-blue sky, 2611 px original.
why_kept: High resolution, plain sky, both tips visible; mild bank noted.
species_check: In Commons category 'Falco peregrinus in flight' (or Commons description says Peregrine); peregrine field marks (black helmet/malar, barred or streaked underparts, barred tail) confirmed on 3.3x crop of head; no kestrel/hobby/other falcon features.

author: Paul Balfe
symmetry_note: FLAP PHASE: top of the upstroke / braking posture, head-on from below. Wings raised above the body plane with wrists high and hand wings drooping outward, feet dropped. Wings symmetric (left:right about 1.1); tail mostly hidden behind the body. Pale blue gradient sky.
why_kept: Clear, symmetric raised-wing flap phase for the flap set.
species_check: In Commons category 'Falco peregrinus in flight' (or Commons description says Peregrine); peregrine field marks (black helmet/malar, barred or streaked underparts, barred tail) confirmed on 4.7x crop of head; no kestrel/hobby/other falcon features.

author: Juan Lacruz
subspecies_or_sex_if_stated: not stated (adult plumage; Spain, same photographer and sequence as the Flying Peregrine image)
symmetry_note: FLAP PHASE: mid-upstroke seen from below and the side. Near/upper wing raised and bunched with primaries folded together; far/lower wing swept down and back and fully extended. Strongly asymmetric: do NOT use for symmetric proportions. Tail narrowly fanned. Uniform blue sky, 1938 px.
why_kept: Sharp mid-flap reference (one wing up, one down) on plain sky.
species_check: In Commons category 'Falco peregrinus in flight'; description says Peregrine Falcon; black helmet and malar, barred underparts and barred tail visible at full frame.

author: Juan Lacruz
subspecies_or_sex_if_stated: not stated (adult; Castilla y Leon, Spain)
symmetry_note: FLAP PHASE (re-labelled after zoom review; first judged a glide): upper wing is raised with its primaries bunched and pointing up, lower wing swept down and back, so this is a mid-upstroke or roll rather than a symmetric glide. Shoulder-to-tip about 715 vs 790 px. Tail partly fanned. Very high resolution (2736 px), uniform blue sky.
why_kept: Highest-resolution mid-flap (upstroke) feather detail; not usable as a symmetric reference.
species_check: In Commons category 'Falco peregrinus in flight' (or Commons description says Peregrine); peregrine field marks (black helmet/malar, barred or streaked underparts, barred tail) confirmed on 2.3x crop of head, full-frame head profile shows malar; no kestrel/hobby/other falcon features.

author: Kytabu
symmetry_note: FLAP PHASE, LOW CONFIDENCE: head-on from below-front with a bank (left wing about 40 pct longer than right in the image). Both wings arched downward from the shoulder and swept back, tail fanned, feet tucked and bird nose-on, consistent with a lowered-wing or early-downstroke posture, but could equally be a banked arched glide. Wingtips curve back. Pale cloud-sky background, 2202 px.
why_kept: Only head-on lowered-wing example with clean sky; phase label uncertain, banked, so not for symmetric measurements.
species_check: In Commons category 'Falco peregrinus in flight' (or Commons description says Peregrine); peregrine field marks (black helmet/malar, barred or streaked underparts, barred tail) confirmed on 2.4x crop of head/tail; no kestrel/hobby/other falcon features.
